about: The colours the approved designs use that are not in icon_kit.py. icon_kit.py (LOOK and HUES, and the muted tones it draws from each hue) is the rest of the palette and is read by tools/check_palette.py, not copied here. To add a colour: put it here with what it is for and where it is used, and say why in the commit.
status: Written from the code on 2026-11-26. Ian approved the plan (a palette taken from the icon kit, a checker, a baseline for the old colours) the same day; the swatch sheet has not been looked at by him yet.

workbench.title: The Workbench
workbench.role: The quiet header design (option 3): the colours the Workbench adds to the kit's. The last four are the groups of the toolbox: the letter chip of a block and the swatch. Its body grey and its ink are the kit's.

colours.name: block edge
colours.use: The edge of a block's bar and body on the canvas

colours.name: wire navy
colours.use: The wires between blocks and the dots they end in

colours.name: Analysis Systems
colours.use: The letter chip of a block and the toolbox swatch

colours.use: The letter chip of a block and the toolbox swatch

ribbon.title: The ribbon
ribbon.role: The Annotator's ribbon, which the Trainer window uses too (design A): a pressed button.

colours.name: pressed fill
colours.use: The background of a checked ribbon button

colours.name: pressed edge
colours.use: The border of a checked ribbon button

viewport.title: The 3D view
viewport.role: How a part looks in the part, assembly and 3D simulation windows (planning/design/viewport): a neutral grey body, an orange outline under the cursor, a blue fill on what is selected. All three are settings in File > Settings > 3D View; these are their defaults.

colours.name: part grey
colours.use: The colour of a part or component that has no colour of its own (60 % grey)

colours.name: hover orange
colours.use: The outline of the face, edge or point under the cursor, and of a selected edge or point

colours.name: select blue
colours.use: The fill of a selected face or body
